newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador plans to spur economy with housing program.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador plans to spur economy with housing program.

text.p: Ecuador's popular housing plan will pump new life into the country's economy, Urban Development and Housing Minister Victor Sicouret said Tuesday.
"I think this will be a historic plan that will mean a lot to the people. People are skeptical because in the past promises were broken," he told Reuters.
President Abdala Bucaram plans to boost construction of homes to an annual 50,000 during his four-year term, against a yearly average of 6,000 since 1965.
The housing plan, 75 percent of which is subsidized by the state, also aims to create 600,000 jobs yearly.
"If we foment domestic savings and the construction industry takes off, its multiplying effect will energize the national economy," said Sicouret.
He said he had discussed the issue with Bucaram's special advisor Domingo Cavallo, the former Argentine economy minister.

Ecuador, with a population of 11.4 million, has a housing shortage of 1.2 million. But activity in the construction sector slowed by 0.5 percent in the first three months of 1996, according to official data.
To sign up for the new housing program poor citizens must pay approximately $15 (50,000 sucres) each month for 20 years or until they have paid a fourth of their home's total average cost of $4,000.
Homes which haven't been subsidized by the government will also be available for lower middle class citizens at a cost of up to $13,681.
Sicouret said the homes would be built by the private sector and government subsidies will amount to $150 million yearly, or 0.85 percent of the country's gross domestic product.
The homes, measuring 36 square meters (360 square feet) each, will cost a total $800 million and will be financed by an Inter-American Development Bank loan of between $400 and $500 million.
Bucaram, who took office July 7, is expected to formally announce the plan Friday, fulfilling one of his campaign promises.
